title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq led stocks higher Friday (+1.2%), with the S&P 500 up 0.7% and the Dow up 0.5% (+250 pts), as investors bet a weak September jobs report (just 29,000 jobs added, unemployment ticking up to 4.2%) keeps the Fed from reversing course on rate cuts.
Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield drifted back up to ~5.3%, not far below this week's 24-year highs; French 10-year yields remain near 2008-era levels amid the country's fiscal turmoil.
Markets: Crude oil fell 1.9% to $91.11/bbl after the G-7 agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves, easing (for now) the threat of a U.S. diesel export ban.
Companies: Anthropic is reportedly targeting a mega IPO before the Thanksgiving holiday (Bloomberg).
Companies: OpenAI fired three researchers for allegedly sharing confidential information with outside evaluators, amid growing internal tension over AI safety policy at frontier labs.

Macro/Policy: The Trump administration is still weighing a diesel export ban (or a softer cap) as pump prices spike nationally to ~$6.53/gallon, up from $3.75 a year ago; officials remain divided on the move.
Macro/Policy: France's fiscal crisis deepens — Scope Ratings downgraded the country to A+ as PM Lecornu's government readies a 2027 budget with ~€54B in spending cuts ahead of a Nov. 17 vote.
